title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page compares the production budget for films with its worldwide revenue. Figure 1 plots budget on the x-axis and revenue on the y-axis.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (millions)")
plt.ylabel("Global revenue (millions)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Budget and Global Revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page compares the runtime of each filmwith its IMDb rating. Figure 1 plots runtime on the x-axis and rating on the y-axis.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime and IMDb rating





This shows the mean IMDb rating by decade.

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10
films.groupby("decade")["imdb_rating"].mean().round(2)

title: Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

The Bond films in this dataset go from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Global revenue (millions)")
plt.show()
